title: Articles
description: Learn articles for Grade 6: a vs an (by sound), the definite article 'the', and the zero article — with rules, exceptions, bilingual notes, examples, practice and tests.

topics.title: A or An — Listen to the Sound
topics.concept:
The choice between a and an depends on the sound of the next word, not its spelling.

  • Use a before a consonant sound: a cat, a tree.
  • Use an before a vowel sound: an egg, an idea.

The clever exceptions all come from sound:

  • a university, a European, a one-rupee coin — these begin with a 'y' or 'w' consonant sound.
  • an hour, an honest man, an MLA — the first letter is silent or sounds like a vowel.

a university — it begins with a 'yoo' (consonant) sound.

recap: a before a consonant sound; an before a vowel sound
Judge by sound, not the first letter (an hour, a university)
Silent letters change the choice (an honest man)

topics.title: The Definite Article & the Zero Article
topics.concept:
Use the when the noun is specific or already known:

  • Something mentioned before: I have a pen. The pen is red.
  • Unique things: the sun, the moon, the sky.
  • Superlatives: the tallest boy.
  • Rivers, seas, mountain ranges: the Ganga, the Himalayas.

Use no article (zero article) with:

  • Uncountable/abstract nouns in general: I love music. Honesty pays.
  • Plural nouns in general: Dogs are loyal.
  • Most proper nouns, languages, meals, games: Hindi, breakfast, chess.

examples.problem: Add an article if needed: ___ Mount Everest is ___ highest peak.
examples.solution: (no article) Mount Everest is the highest peak. — single mountains take no article, but superlatives take 'the'.

examples.problem: Article or zero? She plays ___ chess after ___ dinner.
examples.solution: (no article) chess after (no article) dinner — games and meals take the zero article.

recap: Zero article with general uncountables, general plurals, languages, meals, games
First mention a/an → later mention the

questions.explanation: Abstract noun in general → zero article.

questions.q: 'I bought a pen. ___ pen is blue.'
Choose the fully correct option: 'She is ___ honest and ___ hardworking girl.'
Spot the error: 'The Mount Abu is a beautiful hill station.'
questions.explanation: Single mountains/hills take no article: 'Mount Abu'.

questions.q: Fill in: 'He returned after ___ year, ___ wiser man.'
Which sentence needs NO article in the blank? '____ patience is a virtue.'
questions.explanation: Abstract noun in general → zero article.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'He is the best player of a team.'
questions.explanation: A specific team known from context takes 'the': 'of the team'.

questions.q: Choose: '____ Eiffel Tower is in ____ France.'
questions.explanation: Famous buildings take 'the'; most country names take no article.
Both 'honest' and 'MLA' begin with vowel sounds → 'an'.

questions.q: Choose the correct article use: 'The rich should help ___ poor.'
questions.explanation: 'the + adjective' (the poor) refers to a class of people.

outcomes: Explain the difference between a, an and the
Choose a or an by the sound that follows
Use the for specific or unique nouns
Know when to use no article (zero article)

intro.en: Articles are the little words a, an and the that come before nouns. A and an are indefinite (any one), while the is definite (a particular one). "I saw a dog" means any dog; "I saw the dog" means a specific one we both know.
intro.hi: उपपद / Articles छोटे शब्द a, an और the हैं जो संज्ञा से पहले आते हैं। a/an अनिश्चित (कोई एक) होते हैं, जबकि the निश्चित (कोई विशेष) होता है। "I saw a dog" = कोई भी कुत्ता; "I saw the dog" = एक विशेष कुत्ता।

real_life.situation:
You tell a story:

You: I bought a book and an umbrella. The book was about the sun.
real_life.why: The first time, the things are new, so we use a/an. The second time we already know which book — so we switch to the. And the sun is unique, so it always takes 'the'.

quick_test.explanation: The choice depends on the SOUND that follows (an hour, a university).

common_mistakes.right: (no article) Honesty is the best policy.
common_mistakes.note: Abstract nouns in general take no article.

common_mistakes.wrong: I had a breakfast at the noon.
common_mistakes.note: Meals and 'noon' take the zero article.

reading.passage: Ria is a hardworking student at a famous school. She wants to be an engineer. Every evening, after dinner, she studies under the bright light of a lamp. The book she likes most is about the stars and the planets. Honesty and patience are her best qualities.

questions.answer: 'engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'.
The stars are specific/known things being referred to; many sources also treat them as unique.

questions.q: Which two nouns take no article in the passage and why?
questions.answer: Honesty and patience — abstract nouns used in a general sense take the zero article.

speaking: I saw an elephant at the zoo.
The sun is very bright today.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences about your favourite place, using a, an, the and one zero-article noun.
writing.example: I love the beach near my city. A cool breeze blows there. Peace fills my heart.

micro_quiz.explanation: Uncountable noun in general → zero article.

options: He is a M.A. and an European.
He is an M.A. and a European.
He is a M.A. and a European.
He is an M.A. and an European.
challenge.explanation: 'M.A.' starts with a vowel sound ('em') → an; 'European' starts with 'yoo' → a.
Single mountains take no article: 'Mount Everest', not 'the Mount Everest'.

challenge.q: Identify the error: 'The patience is the key to the success.'
options: Drop both 'the' before patience and success
challenge.explanation: Abstract nouns 'patience' and 'success' used generally take no article.
